answer: Start with the archive, not the applicant. Insurance claim history with underwriter attestation means the applicant shows claims logged over years and held by the underwriter, and the archive belongs to an office that answers to the law. The beacon of the entry is its age: it was filed before this epoch existed, so planting it now would need a corrupt clerk or a time machine. A farm needs a hundred such entries, and the jetty of the hundredth is the same as the first — a visit, a fee, a stamp. The onyx is the cross-check: two offices, one name, one story.
